overview: The particle packet is the one clientbound cosmetic packet that anticheats actively generate. Kauri, FlopAC, Artemis, Daedalus and intave all construct and send S2A (or its PacketEvents equivalent) to draw debug overlays: hitbox cuboids, rays and collision boxes during testing and at flag time. Artemis additionally ships a full read/write wrapper so the packet can be parsed and re-emitted by its pipeline. No anticheat flags S2A as a cheat signal; the corpus treats it as an output channel, not an input.

checks.name: Debug particle visualization (Kauri / FlopAC / Daedalus / intave)
checks.purpose: Render hitboxes, rays and collision boxes to the player's screen by sending particle packets, so staff and developers can see exactly what a check computed.
checks.how_it_works: Kauri's Helper.drawRay and drawCuboid build a WrapperPlayServerParticle (the PacketEvents S2A equivalent) with the ray or box edge positions and send it to the player. FlopAC's MiscUtils does the same through its own WrappedPacketPlayOutWorldParticle wrapper, and its collision box types each implement a draw() that emits particles along their edges. Daedalus submits particle drawing for bounding boxes to a thread pool, and intave spawns villager-happy particles at waypoints via Bukkit spawnParticle, rate-limited per position. The packets are fired on flag, in debug mode, or from dedicated reveal handlers.
checks.detects: Nothing on its own. The visualization is an operator aid layered on top of reach, hitbox and phase checks; it exposes the geometry those checks reason about.
checks.variations: FlopAC MiscUtils.drawRay/drawCuboid mirror Kauri's Helper with its own tinyprotocol wrapper. Daedalus CollisionAssessment sends flame particles for bounding boxes. intave Particles.spawnVillagerHappyParticleAt rate-limits waypoint particles. Artemis BoundingUtil.drawBox uses its GPacketPlayServerWorldParticles wrapper for the same purpose.

checks.name: World particles wrapper (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Give Artemis a full read/write wrapper for the world-particles packet so the pipeline can parse inbound S2A and re-emit particle packets for debug drawing.
checks.how_it_works: GPacketPlayServerWorldParticles implements ReadableBuffer and WriteableBuffer. read() parses the particle type (with a BARRIER fallback on a bad id), the long-distance flag, position, offsets, speed, count and the per-type argument array; write() serializes them back, negating particle arguments on the wire. BoundingUtil.drawBox builds one of these packets per box edge to render debug bounding boxes, and the ProtocolGeneratorDirect registers the class in the generated protocol.
checks.detects: Nothing. The wrapper is bidirectional plumbing: inbound parsing feeds the packet pipeline, outbound construction powers the debug-box renderer.
checks.variations: Artemis also maps SERVER_PLAY + 93 to PacketPlayServerWorldParticles in its repository. FlopAC's WrappedPacketPlayOutWorldParticle covers the same packet for its 1.8 base, and Kauri uses PacketEvents' WrapperPlayServerParticle directly.
